messages:
alex: Quick note: ran the new kernel-selector against a prod trace via replay. p99 ~116ms vs synthetic 98ms.
maya: Can you post the exact commands/config?
alex: Synthetic: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d120s --script=gen.lua http://svc/generate`
Replay: `python replay.py --trace prod-2026-03-10.json --concurrency 200 --open-new-conn`
Numbers: synthetic p99=98ms, replay p99=116ms, medians ~equal.
li: That --open-new-conn sounds bad. Does replay do a full TCP/TLS handshake per request?
alex: Yes, default replay opens new connection per request for fidelity. Didn't expect 18% delta.
sam: TLS handshake can add tens of ms. Also Nagle + small writes add tails without keepalive.
maya: Kernel selector differences? Both set to auto but logs show fused-attn chosen for synthetic, fallback for replay.
alex: perf top during replay spikes in mbedtls_ssl_handshake and sendmsg; GPU utilization lower; KV cache hit rate same.
li: So two factors: client connection churn and different seq-length mix causing different kernel picks.
sam: Replay replays exact prefixes distribution, more short prefixes -> batch seq len mix changes -> selector picks different kernels if it's based on median/percentile.
maya: Let's run (1) replay with persistent connections (`--keepalive`) and (2) synthetic but force new connections (`--new-conn`) and compare.
alex: Results: replay + keepalive -> p99 101ms. synthetic + new-conn -> p99 114ms. So client-side dominates.
li: What about gRPC vs REST? Our synthetic uses REST.
sam: gRPC uses multiplexed HTTP/2 channel so handshake per channel, not per request -> reduces TLS churn.
alex: gRPC replay (single channel) -> p99 99ms, matches synthetic keepalive.
maya: So for apples-to-apples kernel/batching tests we must control client behavior: conn reuse, packetization, Nagle, TLS session reuse.
li: Also note python http pool default size=10 interacts with concurrency; opening new conn per request bypasses pooling and incurs cost.
sam: Ops checklist:
- Default to connection reuse unless testing handshake costs.
- Document pool sizes and client stack (requests/aiohttp/grpc).
- Add replay option to preserve original conn reuse patterns.
- Add synthetic mode emulating TCP gaps and conn open/close.
alex: PR opened to change replay.py default to --keepalive and add --conn-pattern: https://git/repo/pull/472 (benchbot: label perf-regression)
maya: Runtime: add kernel-selection debug flag to log chosen kernel + reason per batch.
li: Add KV cache profiling hook to verify misses not correlated with conn churn.
sam: Add CI matrix: synthetic (keepalive), replay (keepalive), synthetic (new-conn), gRPC (single channel) — capture p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.
alex: I'll add CI. For now default to gRPC single-channel for high-concurrency benchmarks; update docs.
maya: Posting summary to #eng-runtime to avoid chasing kernel changes first.
benchbot: Reminder: run new benchmark matrix on feature branch tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
alex: Next steps: replay defaults PR, kernel logging, CI job. Assign @maya @alex @li.
maya: I'll own kernel logging. li: KV profiling. alex: replay changes.
li: On it.
